learning_objective: ⌚ Enjoy a hilarious satire on the human obsession with timepieces and the endless cycle of trying to fix things that aren't broken!

main_concepts.simple_explanation: The narrator owns a beautiful, perfect watch that keeps time faultlessly for 18 months. He compares its absolute reliability to an infallible judgment. However, one night, he forgets to wind it, which sets off a chain of disastrous events.

Panicking after the watch stops, he takes it to a jeweler to set the time. The jeweler cruelly adjusts the 'regulator'. From that day on, the watch starts gaining time relentlessly, running so fast it leaves the rest of the world behind.

He takes it to another watchmaker to slow it down. Now, the watch becomes miserably slow. It ticks like a dying man and falls days behind the actual calendar. The narrator starts living in 'yesterday'.

After more repairs, the watch starts acting crazy. It runs fine for half a day, then barks like a machine gun, and finally stops completely. It sneezes, wheezes, and shows multiple erratic personalities.

An old watchmaker finally tells him the watch's internal machinery is completely ruined. The narrator realizes a bitter truth: all unsuccessful shoemakers, gunsmiths, and blacksmiths end up becoming 'watchmakers' just to ruin good watches!

fun_activity.title: 🎭 Personify an Object
fun_activity.instructions: Mark Twain talks about his watch as if it were a living person with a 'constitution' and a 'pulse'. Try writing a 3-line paragraph complaining about your smartphone or laptop acting like a stubborn, moody teenager!

exam_tips: 📌 Twain uses 'Personification' extensively. He describes the watch suffering from 'swelling of the stomach' and having 'symptoms'. Mention this in your stylistic analysis.
📌 The underlying theme of the essay is a satire on the incompetence of self-proclaimed 'experts' (the watchmakers).
📌 Notice the hyperbole (exaggeration) used when the watch gains so much time that it enters 'next week' while the world is still in the present.
quick_recap: ⭐ Forgetting to wind the watch was the narrator's only original mistake.
⭐ Each time a watchmaker 'fixed' the watch, the repair bill grew larger, and the watch's condition grew worse.
⭐ The essay is a classic example of Mark Twain's deadpan, exaggerated American humor.
